subject: Private deployment: onramp certification, VPC peering & appliance acceptance sprint
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment: onramp certification, VPC peering & appliance acceptance sprint

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, I'm putting together the checklist and a short ops sprint we can run the week of 02/14 to finish VPC peering, private endpoint setup, and appliance acceptance testing. High-level asks from your side:

- Confirm one or two CIDR blocks we can use for the VPC peering (we recommended a /20 or larger).
- Provide a CPE contact and a time window for the initial ingress test (we typically need a 2-hour window for full KV cache warm-up and end-to-end smoke tests).
- Share the customer network inventory (attached CSV stub) and the IP allowlist for private endpoints.

I've attached a short network inventory template and our MVP checklist (acme_mvp_network_checklist.xlsx) — these are the fields we need filled to generate the on-prem appliance manifest and certs.

Proposed sprint milestones:
1) Preflight & inventory completed (we get your filled CSV) — target 2/10
2) VPC peering + route/ACL verification — 2/14 (2-hour maintenance window)
3) Private endpoints (DNS & cert install) — 2/15
4) Appliance delivery & manifest install (on your staging rack) — 2/17
5) Acceptance tests & go/no-go — 2/18

Can you confirm those dates/times or propose alternatives? If useful, I can loop in our implementation lead (Camila) and CS manager (Marissa) to own the acceptance checklist.

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear plan. Couple quick clarifications from our infra team:

- CIDR: We can allocate 10.48.0.0/20 for the peering; will that work?
- Private endpoints: We use wildcard internal certs managed by our PKI team; do you need SANs for the appliance hostname or will the IP-based allowlist be sufficient for the initial tests?
- Appliance manifest: We have a change freeze on 2/17 for our staging cluster (security patch window). Can we shift the appliance delivery and acceptance to 2/20 and acceptance tests to 2/21?

I attached a rough copy of our current network inventory export (acme_network_inventory.csv) — it's missing a couple of VLAN IDs, which we can add by tomorrow.

If Camila and Marissa are joining, please include any readiness checks they need to run on our side ahead of the VPC peering.

Best,
Dana

Subject: Fwd: Private deployment: onramp certification, VPC peering & appliance acceptance sprint

Team —

Forwarding the thread from Acme. Requesting Camila to take implementation lead on the sprint and Marissa to own customer acceptance criteria. Key constraints: Acme proposes 10.48.0.0/20 and wants to push appliance delivery to 2/20 due to a staging change freeze.

Camila — can you:
- Review the attached inventory and confirm whether the /20 fits our routing profile and whether we need a separate management CIDR for the appliance.
- Confirm the SAN vs IP allowlist approach for private endpoints; if we need SANs we'll need the fully-qualified hostnames by 2/13 to include in the cert CSR.
- Draft a short 30-min preflight runbook for their infra/pki team (checklist items: NTP sync, DNS resolution for private endpoints, firewall rules, MTU checks, and baseline token throughput test).

Marissa — please prepare a one-page acceptance matrix we can share with Acme that maps the acceptance tests to pass/fail criteria and ownership. I'll align the sprint dates to the 2/20 delivery window.

Attachments: acme_network_inventory.csv (customer export), acme_mvp_network_checklist.xlsx (template), redwood-onprem-appliance-manifest.pdf (appliance manifest template)

Thanks — looping you both in to coordinate directly with Dana and Tom.

Ben

--
Ben Carter

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Liu <dana.liu@acmehealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Feb 2028 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment: onramp certification, VPC peering & appliance acceptance sprint

Hi all —

Thanks Ben, and thanks Dana for the inventory export. Quick read and next steps from my side:

1) CIDR: 10.48.0.0/20 is acceptable for the peering. We'll ask for a separate /24 for appliance mgmt (10.48.240.0/24) to avoid overlapping NAT ranges during kernel live-migration tests. Please confirm if Acme can carve that out.

2) Certs vs IP allowlist: For initial smoke we'll support IP allowlist only, but for production traffic we require an FQDN SAN on the cert. If Acme can provide the hostnames for the appliance (recommended pattern: appliance01.acme.internal), we can provision the CSR during the 2/13-2/14 window. Without SANs some automated health checks will be limited.

3) Preflight runbook (draft highlights):
- Verify NTP and time drift <= 500ms across nodes
- DNS resolution for appliance hostnames and private endpoints from their jumpbox
- TCP connectivity on port 443 and gRPC port 6200 from the expected CIDR
- Verify MTU >= 1400 end-to-end (we've seen fragmentation at 1300)
- Confirm that BGP/route propagation (if used) is stable for at least 10 minutes before tests
- Appliance manifest install: confirm available /var/lib/redwood capacity >= 120GB

4) Timeline adjustments: 2/20 delivery and 2/21 acceptance tests works on our side. I'll schedule two 90-minute windows on 2/21 (09:00-10:30 PT and 13:00-14:30 PT) for the acceptance runs — please let me know which one works for Acme.

5) Action items for Acme:
- Confirm management CIDR 10.48.240.0/24 by EOD 2/10
- Provide appliance FQDNs by 2/13 if you want cert SANs provisioned
- Populate the missing VLAN IDs in the inventory CSV and re-send

I'll attach a short preflight checklist and a Jenkins job link we use to run the baseline token throughput test in staging. If anyone wants to jump on a screen-share to walk through the checklist, I'm available tomorrow between 11:00-13:00 PT.

Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
